output.brief:
The rise in cancellations is mostly not a pricing problem. It is a Quillbook invoicing fault. Quillbook retired an old interface on 30 March. Since then the connector has silently dropped or duplicated invoices. 1,212 of 1,900 Quillbook accounts were affected, and 34% of those have cancelled, against 8% of unaffected accounts. Quillbook accounts churn at about 6% a month whether or not they got the price rise, which includes Founders accounts that were never repriced. Accounts with no connector, repriced or not, churn at about 1.9%, which is normal. The earlier price-size pattern is explained by larger accounts being more likely to use Quillbook. The fault is logged only as a warning, so the health panel does not show it. I'm fairly confident, about 85%.

Next steps:
- Make the Quillbook fix (move to v3, 3–4 weeks) the top engineering priority.
- Contact every Quillbook account, including those that cancelled, to correct invoices.
- Keep the duplicate-invoice hold on.
- Don't roll back the price on 1 September.
- Don't start the Tallymarsh rebuild yet. Review its log first, since its numbers are tiny and within normal variation.
- Make the warning-level connector events visible on the health panel.
